Weighted cancellation for complex phases

An oscillatory integral can be small for two different reasons. A changing real phase produces cancellation; a positive imaginary phase produces damping. The quantity that combines them is We prove an estimate that keeps the exact powers of this quantity, even when it approaches zero. The argument uses only finitely many derivatives. An integral version of the estimate also applies when the resulting singular weights are integrable.
